title: How to be charming
paragraphs: Life isn‘t fair. Some people just seem blessed with the ability to effortlessly charm anyone they meet. You know the kind of person, the one who can strike up a conversation with a complete stranger and end up with a new friend or business lead. How do they do it?

Well, it might seem like a magical power, but in fact there are a number of factors at work. So, can you learn to develop superhuman charm? The answer is: to a large extent, yes you can. But first, the bad news. Scientists have found that people initially judge each other based purely on physical appearance. With just a fleeting glimpse of a face, people make snap judgements about each other’s likeability, trustworthiness and confidence, according to Alexander Todorov, professor of psychology at Princeton University.

How to counteract this? There‘s one incredibly simple tool: your smile. Todorov told the BBC that people perceive a smiling face as “more trustworthy, warmer and sociable”. It sounds like common sense, doesn’t it? Smile and others will smile with you.

What other tricks might we have up our sleeves? Former FBI agent Jack Schafer has been trained in how to influence people. He told BBC Capital: “Our brains are always surveying the environment for friend or foe signals.” Three things we can do to signal that we are not a threat are to: raise our eyebrows quickly, tilt our heads slightly, and, once again, to smile.

So we‘ve looked at body language, but of course what you say is hugely important too, unless you want to just stand there grinning foolishly. Here Schafer recommends that “the golden rule of friendship is if you make people feel good about themselves, they’re going to like you.” In other words, you need to show interest in them, instead of talking about yourself and all your wonderful achievements. And while you‘re chatting, remember this: another way of showing interest is to mirror their physical position.

Another way to form a connection? Find common ground. Suzanne de Janasz, a professor of management with Seattle University, says that charming people are particularly adept at seeking out shared interests or experiences to help them build rapport. Simple things like asking where someone‘s from really can open up a discussion and allow you to find areas in common. And if all else fails, you can fall back on that most British of topics: the weather. Glorious day, isn’t it?

vocabulary.entry: blessed with [phr.] /ˈblesɪd wɪð/ 拥有；赋有（某种运气、特质等）
vocabulary.example: She is blessed with a wonderful singing voice.
vocabulary.translation: 她拥有一副美妙的歌喉。

vocabulary.entry: charm [v.] /tʃɑːm/ 吸引；迷住
vocabulary.example: His friendly manner charmed everyone at the party.
vocabulary.translation: 他友善的举止迷住了派对上的每个人。

vocabulary.entry: strike up [phr.] /straɪk ʌp/ 开始（交谈、友谊等）
vocabulary.example: He struck up a conversation with the person next to him.
vocabulary.translation: 他和旁边的人开始聊了起来。

vocabulary.entry: fleeting [adj.] /ˈfliːtɪŋ/ 短暂的；飞逝的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: She caught a fleeting glimpse of the famous actor.
vocabulary.translation: 她匆匆瞥了那位著名演员一眼。

vocabulary.entry: snap judgements [n. pl.] /snæp ˈdʒʌdʒmənts/ 快速判断；草率判断 (口语；单数: snap judgement)
vocabulary.example: It‘s unfair to make snap judgements about people.
vocabulary.translation: 对人做出草率判断是不公平的。

vocabulary.entry: counteract [v.] /ˌkaʊntərˈækt/ 抵消；对抗 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Drinking water can counteract the effects of dehydration.
vocabulary.translation: 喝水可以抵消脱水的影响。

vocabulary.entry: perceive [v.] /pəˈsiːv/ 认为；理解 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: How do you perceive the current political situation?
vocabulary.translation: 你如何看待当前的政治局势？

vocabulary.entry: tricks [n. pl.] /trɪks/ 窍门；技巧 (单数: trick)
vocabulary.example: Here are some tricks to help you remember new vocabulary.
vocabulary.translation: 这里有一些帮助你记住新词汇的窍门。

vocabulary.entry: mirror [v.] /ˈmɪrə/ 模仿；映照 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: People often unconsciously mirror the body language of those they like.
vocabulary.translation: 人们常常无意识地模仿他们喜欢的人的肢体语言。

vocabulary.entry: adept at [phr.] /əˈdept æt/ 擅长；善于 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: She is adept at solving difficult problems.
vocabulary.translation: 她擅长解决难题。

vocabulary.entry: rapport [n.] /ræˈpɔː/ 融洽的关系；和谐 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The teacher has a good rapport with her students.
vocabulary.translation: 这位老师和她的学生们关系很融洽。

vocabulary.entry: fall back on [phr.] /fɔːl bæk ɒn/ 求助于；依靠
vocabulary.example: If the plan fails, we can fall back on our savings.
vocabulary.translation: 如果计划失败，我们可以依靠我们的积蓄。

vocabulary.entry: effortlessly [adv.] /ˈefətləsli/ 毫不费力地；轻松地
vocabulary.example: He solved the puzzle effortlessly.
vocabulary.translation: 他毫不费力地解开了谜题。

vocabulary.entry: likeability [n.] /ˌlaɪkəˈbɪləti/ 可爱；讨人喜欢 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Her likeability makes her popular with everyone.
vocabulary.translation: 她的讨人喜欢使她受到大家的欢迎。

vocabulary.entry: trustworthiness [n.] /ˈtrʌstwɜːðinəs/ 可信赖；可靠 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Trustworthiness is an important quality in a leader.
vocabulary.translation: 可信赖是领导者的一项重要品质。

vocabulary.entry: sociable [adj.] /ˈsəʊʃəbəl/ 好交际的；友善的
vocabulary.example: He is a sociable person who enjoys meeting new people.
vocabulary.translation: 他是个好交际的人，喜欢结识新朋友。

vocabulary.entry: surveying [v.] /səˈveɪɪŋ/ 审视；调查 (原形: survey)
vocabulary.example: She was surveying the room, looking for a familiar face.
vocabulary.translation: 她审视着房间，寻找一张熟悉的面孔。

vocabulary.entry: tilt [v.] /tɪlt/ 倾斜；歪斜
vocabulary.example: He tilted his head to one side as he listened.
vocabulary.translation: 他听的时候把头歪向一边。

vocabulary.entry: glorious [adj.] /ˈɡlɔːriəs/ 壮丽的；极好的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: We had a glorious day at the beach.
vocabulary.translation: 我们在海滩度过了美好的一天。

vocabulary.entry: initially [adv.] /ɪˈnɪʃəli/ 最初；起初
vocabulary.example: Initially, I didn‘t like the idea, but now I think it’s great.
vocabulary.translation: 起初我不喜欢这个主意，但现在我觉得它很棒。

sentences.chinese: 生活是不公平的。

sentences.chinese: 有些人似乎就是拥有一种能力，能够毫不费力地吸引他们遇到的每一个人。

sentences.chinese: 你知道那种人，就是那种能够和一个完全陌生的人开始一段对话，最后还能结交到新朋友或者获得商业线索的人。

sentences.english: How do they do it?
sentences.chinese: 他们是怎么做到的呢？

sentences.english: Well, it might seem like a magical power, but in fact there are a number of factors at work.
sentences.chinese: 嗯，这可能看起来像是一种神奇的力量，但实际上有许多因素在起作用。

sentences.english: So, can you learn to develop superhuman charm?
sentences.chinese: 那么，你能学会培养出超凡的魅力吗？

sentences.english: The answer is: to a large extent, yes you can.
sentences.chinese: 答案是：在很大程度上，你可以。

sentences.english: But first, the bad news.
sentences.chinese: 但首先，有个坏消息。

sentences.english: Scientists have found that people initially judge each other based purely on physical appearance.
sentences.chinese: 科学家们发现，人们最初纯粹是根据外貌来评判彼此的。

sentences.english: With just a fleeting glimpse of a face, people make snap judgements about each other’s likeability, trustworthiness and confidence, according to Alexander Todorov, professor of psychology at Princeton University.
sentences.chinese: 普林斯顿大学的心理学教授亚历山大·托多罗夫表示，仅仅通过匆匆瞥过一张脸，人们就能对彼此的好感度、可信度和自信程度做出快速判断。

sentences.english: How to counteract this?
sentences.chinese: 如何抵消这种情况呢？

sentences.english: There‘s one incredibly simple tool: your smile.
sentences.chinese: 有一个极其简单的办法：你的微笑。

sentences.english: Todorov told the BBC that people perceive a smiling face as “more trustworthy, warmer and sociable”.
sentences.chinese: 托多罗夫告诉英国广播公司，人们认为一张微笑的脸“更值得信赖、更温暖且更善于社交”。

sentences.english: It sounds like common sense, doesn’t it?
sentences.chinese: 这听起来像是常识，不是吗？

sentences.english: Smile and others will smile with you.
sentences.chinese: 你微笑，别人也会对你微笑。

sentences.english: What other tricks might we have up our sleeves?
sentences.chinese: 我们还可能有哪些窍门呢？

sentences.english: Former FBI agent Jack Schafer has been trained in how to influence people.
sentences.chinese: 前联邦调查局特工杰克·谢弗接受过如何影响他人的培训。

sentences.english: He told BBC Capital: “Our brains are always surveying the environment for friend or foe signals.”
sentences.chinese: 他告诉BBC资本频道：“我们的大脑总是在审视周围环境，寻找是朋友还是敌人的信号。”

sentences.english: Three things we can do to signal that we are not a threat are to: raise our eyebrows quickly, tilt our heads slightly, and, once again, to smile.
sentences.chinese: 为了表明我们没有威胁，我们可以做三件事：快速扬起眉毛、微微倾斜头部，还有，再次强调，微笑。

sentences.english: So we‘ve looked at body language, but of course what you say is hugely important too, unless you want to just stand there grinning foolishly.
sentences.chinese: 所以我们已经探讨了肢体语言，但当然，你说的话也非常重要，除非你想只是站在那里傻乎乎地咧嘴笑。

sentences.english: Here Schafer recommends that “the golden rule of friendship is if you make people feel good about themselves, they’re going to like you.”
sentences.chinese: 谢弗在这里建议说：“友谊的黄金法则是，如果你能让人们自我感觉良好，他们就会喜欢你。”

sentences.english: In other words, you need to show interest in them, instead of talking about yourself and all your wonderful achievements.
sentences.chinese: 换句话说，你需要表现出对他们的兴趣，而不是谈论你自己和你所有了不起的成就。

sentences.english: And while you‘re chatting, remember this: another way of showing interest is to mirror their physical position.
sentences.chinese: 而且当你聊天的时候，记住这一点：另一种表现出兴趣的方式是模仿他们的身体姿势。

sentences.english: Another way to form a connection?
sentences.chinese: 另一种建立联系的方式呢？

sentences.english: Find common ground.
sentences.chinese: 寻找共同点。

sentences.english: Suzanne de Janasz, a professor of management with Seattle University, says that charming people are particularly adept at seeking out shared interests or experiences to help them build rapport.
sentences.chinese: 西雅图大学的管理学教授苏珊娜·德·亚纳兹说，有魅力的人特别擅长找出共同的兴趣或经历，以此来帮助他们建立融洽的关系。

sentences.english: Simple things like asking where someone‘s from really can open up a discussion and allow you to find areas in common.
sentences.chinese: 像问问别人来自哪里这样简单的事情，真的可以开启一场讨论，让你找到共同之处。

sentences.english: And if all else fails, you can fall back on that most British of topics: the weather.
sentences.chinese: 而且如果其他方法都行不通，你还可以求助于最具英国特色的话题：天气。

sentences.english: Glorious day, isn’t it?
sentences.chinese: 今天天气真好，不是吗？
